Subject: MAP: cost assumptions & token economics for POC

Soojin —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We loved the latency and the routing ideas; our procurement and ML teams asked for a short MAP that includes the cost gating items (tokens/$, caching assumptions, batching SLOs) so we can validate feasibility for a 6-week POC.

High-level ask from our side:
- Baseline tokens per USD for the model you showed (40k context), and sensitivities at 2x/5x load
- How prefix/KV caching will work during spike periods and whether warm-up costs are material
- Typical batching assumptions (batch size distribution, latency impact) and which knobs we can tune for latency vs cost
- A suggested eval plan (prompt set, metric thresholds) and a mutual action timeline to close (POC -> pilot -> commit)

Can you send a worksheet with the numbers and a short MAP timeline? Procurement also wants a sense of credits for the POC and the SOC2 evidence checklist.

Appreciate it — can do a call if needed.

Kelly
Kelly Harper
Head of ML Platforms, Cerebro Labs

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@cerebrolabs.com>

Subject: Re: MAP cost gate & QA worksheet — tokens/$, batching, caching

Kelly —

Thanks for the clear asks. I attached a concise worksheet (Cerebro-MAP-v1.xlsx) and a short assumptions brief (token-batching-assumptions.pdf) that outline the unit economics and gating questions. High-level summary up front:

1) Baseline tokens per USD (hosted, standard model variant): ~120k tokens / $1 for seq length mix weighted toward 512 avg.
   - 2x traffic -> ~95k tokens / $1 (due to smaller batching efficiency drop)
   - 5x traffic -> ~70k tokens / $1 (bulk of increase comes from KV warm-up and decreased batching)

2) Caching assumptions
   - Prefix/KV cache reduces repeated prefix cost by ~40–65% depending on hit rate; assume 30% hit rate conservative for POC
   - Warm-up: first-hour per-user sessions may show ~15–40% higher per-token cost; recommend pre-warming keys during eval if feasible

3) Batching assumptions & latency tradeoffs
   - Default continuous batching with 20ms max latency cap yields average batch size ~8 for this workload; raising cap to 50ms can increase tokens/$ by ~12%
   - We can pin per-route latency SLOs in the MAP and configure a burst policy for peak windows

4) Eval plan & MAP timeline (proposed)
   - Week 0: sign MAP (confirm dataset/prompts + access)
   - Week 1–2: POC ingest + baseline runs (collect token counts, cache hit rates)
   - Week 3: tuning (batch window, cache TTLs, quantization options)
   - Week 4: evaluation & quality regression checks (prompt set, automated evals)
   - Week 5: decision + commercial terms for pilot

Next steps: please confirm the expected concurrent users and typical request distribution (short vs long). I also attached the SOC2-evidence-checklist your procurement asked for — procurement can have it as an artifact.

If useful we can do a 30-min technical sync with Dev (cc'd) and Mateo for eval metrics.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
Attachment: Cerebro-MAP-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet); token-batching-assumptions.pdf (brief)

Thanks, Soojin — this is great and gives us what we need to start internal sign-off. A couple of clarifying points from the ML infra team:

- Concurrent users: expected steady-state ~1200 concurrent API sessions during business hours, spike to ~4k for batch review windows (10–15min, 2x per day).
- Request shape: ~85% short (<512 tokens total), 15% long (>2k tokens) but long requests are often single-threaded and infrequent.
- For KV cache: we can pre-warm the top 2000 keys for the initial evaluation, but we will need to know the per-key warm-up cost in tokens and wall-time so we can budget credits.

Procurement side: procurement@cerebrolabs.com asked whether you can confirm a small POC credit (USD value) and what a softened SLA for POC would look like.

Happy to take the tech sync — propose Friday 10/1 10:00 PT.

Jordan
Jordan Price
Platform Eng — Cerebro Labs

Kelly/Jordan —

Thanks for the sync Friday — summary and agreed gating items attached. Key outcomes and MAP timeline (agreed):

Agreed unit-econ guardrails:
- Baseline tokens/$ (hosted standard): 115k tokens / $1 (conservative for the POC accounting for short/long mix)
- Acceptance gate at decision: tokens/$ must not exceed 90k tokens / $1 at observed 2x load
- Cache hit target for POC: >= 28% (we agreed to instrument and report this daily)

Operational gating & credits:
- Redwood to provide $12,000 POC credit (applied to usage)
- POC SLA: 72-hour support response; critical escalation path documented in SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf

Evaluation plan highlights:
- Week 1: ingest and baseline metrics (token counts, latency, cache hit)
- Week 2: tuning (batch window adjustments, TTLs); Mateo to run automated eval harness and report quality metrics
- Week 3: stability runs and final evaluation; decision meeting end of Week 3 to determine pilot commitment

Action items (owners):
- Cerebro: share list of top 2k keys to pre-warm + dataset of 250 prompt examples (Jordan) — due Mon 10/04
- Redwood Dev (Dev): run a warm-up simulation and return estimated warm-up token cost and expected time by Tue 10/05
- Redwood Commercial (Marissa): share POC credit agreement and short SLA by Tue 10/05
- Redwood Applied ML (Mateo): provide eval harness and baseline metrics report by Wed 10/06

Attachments: Cerebro-MAP-v1.xlsx (MAP worksheet), token-batching-assumptions.pdf, SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf

If that aligns I'll send a final signed MAP doc and HubSpot record (HS-120483) with deliverables. Meeting invite for Friday recurring is attached.

Best regards,
